tools.name: auth.who-am-i
tools.description: Returns the catalog entity and user info for the currently authenticated user. This action requires user credentials and cannot be used with service or unauthenticated credentials.

tools.name: catalog.get-catalog-model-description
tools.description: Returns a markdown formatted description of the current catalog model, including all registered entity kinds, annotations, labels, tags, and relations.

tools.name: catalog.get-catalog-entity
tools.description:
This allows you to get a single entity from the software catalog.
Each entity in the software catalog has a unique name, kind, and namespace. The default namespace is "default".
Each entity is identified by a unique entity reference, which is a string of the form "kind:namespace/name".

kind.description: The kind of the entity to query. If the kind is unknown it can be omitted.

namespace.description: The namespace of the entity to query. If the namespace is unknown it can be omitted.

name.description: The name of the entity to query

tools.name: catalog.validate-entity
tools.description:
This action can be used to validate catalog-info.yaml file contents meant to be used with the software catalog.
      It checks both that the YAML syntax is correct, and that the entity content is valid according to the catalog's rules.

tools.name: catalog.register-entity
tools.description:
Registers one or more entities in the Backstage catalog by creating a Location entity that points to a remote catalog-info.yaml file.

This action is similar to the "Register existing component" flow in the Backstage UI, where you provide a URL to a catalog-info.yaml file describing catalog entities such as Components, Systems, Resources, APIs, Users, and Groups. The action will create a new Location entity that references the provided file; all entities defined within that file will be imported into the catalog.

A unique identifier (locationId) will be returned for the newly created Location. You can use this identifier in the future to unregister or delete the Location and all entities it owns.

locationUrl.description: URL reference to the catalog-info.yaml file that describes the entity to register. For example: https://github.com/backstage/demo/blob/master/catalog-info.yaml

tools.name: catalog.unregister-entity
tools.description:
Unregisters a Location entity and all entities it owns from the Backstage catalog.

This action is similar to the "Unregister location" function in the Backstage UI, where you provide the unique identifier (locationId) of a Location entity. Alternatively, you can provide the URL used to register the location. The action will remove the specified Location from the catalog as well as all entities that were created when the Location was imported.

Once completed, all entities associated with the Location will be deleted from the catalog.

locationId.description: Location ID of the Entity to unregister

locationUrl.description: URL of the catalog-info.yaml file to unregister for example: https://github.com/backstage/demo/blob/master/catalog-info.yaml

type.description: Identifies the entity to unregister. Provide either locationId or locationUrl.

tools.name: catalog.query-catalog-entities

query.description: Entity predicate query. Supports field matching, $all, $any, $not, $exists, $in, $contains, and $hasPrefix operators.

fields.description: Specific fields to include in the response. If not provided, all fields are returned. Each entry is a dot separated path into an entity, e.g. `spec.type`.

limit.description: Maximum number of entities to return at a time.

offset.description: Number of entities to skip before returning results.

field.description: Field to order by. The format is a dot separated path into an entity, e.g. `spec.type`.
Field to order by. The format is a dot separated path into an entity, e.g. `spec.type`.

orderFields.description: Ordering criteria for the results. Can be a single order directive or an array for multi-field sorting.

fields.description: Fields to search within. Each entry is a dot separated path into an entity, e.g. `spec.type`.

cursor.description: Cursor for pagination. This can be used only after the first request with a response containing a cursor. If a cursor is given it takes precedence over `offset`.

tools.name: catalog.refresh-catalog-entity
tools.description:
This allows you to trigger a refresh of a single entity in the software catalog, requeuing it for processing.
This is useful immediately after creating or updating an entity (for example via a scaffolder template invoked by an MCP client) so the new data becomes visible before subsequent actions read it.
Each entity in the software catalog has a unique name, kind, and namespace. If the name alone matches multiple entities, provide the kind (and namespace) to disambiguate.

kind.description: The kind of the entity to refresh, e.g. "Component", "API", "System". If the kind is unknown it can be omitted.

namespace.description: The namespace of the entity to refresh. If the namespace is unknown it can be omitted.

name.description: The name of the entity to refresh.

tools.name: scaffolder.list-scaffolder-tasks
tools.description:
This allows you to list scaffolder tasks that have been created.
Each task has a unique id, specification, and status (one of open, processing, completed, failed, cancelled, skipped).
Each task includes a timestamp for when it was created, and an optional last heartbeat timestamp indicating the most recent activity.
Set owned to true to return only tasks created by the current user; omit or set to false for all tasks the credentials can see.
Filtering by one or multiple statuses is supported. Pagination is supported via limit and offset.

owned.description: If true, return only tasks created by the current user. Requires a user identity.

limit.description: The maximum number of tasks to return for pagination

offset.description: The offset to start from for pagination

status.description: Filter tasks by status, or an array of statuses

tools.name: scaffolder.dry-run-template
tools.description: Dry-runs a scaffolder template to validate it without making changes. Returns success with execution logs, or errors for validation failures.

templateYaml.description: The YAML content of the scaffolder template to validate

path.description: File path relative to template root

files.description: Files required for running the template

tools.name: scaffolder.list-scaffolder-actions
tools.description:
Lists all installed Scaffolder actions.
Each action includes:
- id: The action identifier
- description: What the action does
- schema: Input and output JSON schemas
- examples: Usage examples when available

tools.name: scaffolder.execute-template
tools.description:
Executes a Scaffolder template with its template ref and input parameter values.
The template is run using the credentials provided to this action, and respects any RBAC permissions associated with those credentials.
Returns a taskId that can be used to track execution progress.
Use the catalog.get-catalog-entity action to fetch the Template entity and discover its parameter schema and secrets definition before calling this action.

templateRef.description: The template entity reference to execute, e.g. "template:default/my-template"

values.description: Input parameter values required by the template. Use catalog.get-catalog-entity to discover the required parameters for the template.

secrets.description: Optional secrets to pass to the template execution. Use catalog.get-catalog-entity to discover the secrets definition on the Template entity.

tools.name: scaffolder.get-scaffolder-task-logs
tools.description:
Retrieve the log events for a scaffolder task.
Each log event has a type (log, completion, cancelled, or recovered), a body containing a message and optional step ID and status.
Use the after parameter to fetch only events after a specific event ID for incremental polling.

taskId.description: The ID of the scaffolder task

after.description: Return only log events after this event ID for incremental polling
